input.empty.title: Input is empty
input.empty.explanation: The input contains no data, or only whitespace, so there is nothing to inspect.

remediation.text: Check that the right file was given and that it is not empty.

input.unsupported_format.title: Unsupported input
input.unsupported_format.explanation: This input, or one block in it, is not something this version of Trustsmith inspects. This version inspects X.509 certificates in PEM or DER form. Other PEM blocks, such as private keys or certificate requests, are reported by their label only and are not decoded.

remediation.text: Provide a PEM or DER certificate, or a PEM bundle of certificates.

input.no_certificates.title: No certificates found
input.no_certificates.explanation: The input was read, but it contains no certificate that could be inspected.

remediation.text: Check that the right file was given and that it contains a certificate.

input.malformed_pem.title: Malformed PEM block
input.malformed_pem.explanation: A PEM block could not be decoded: its BEGIN line is invalid, its matching END line is missing, or its contents are not valid base64. The other blocks in the same input are still inspected.

remediation.text: Export the certificate again from its source instead of repairing the file by hand.

input.malformed_der.title: Malformed DER
input.malformed_der.explanation: The input starts like binary DER but is not one valid DER structure.

remediation.text: Export the certificate again from its source, in PEM or DER form.

input.trailing_data.title: Extra data outside certificates
input.trailing_data.explanation: The input contains data that belongs to no certificate, such as text around PEM blocks or bytes after a DER certificate. Strict software may reject files like this.

remediation.text: Remove the extra data if the file is read by strict software.

input.unparseable_certificate.title: Certificate could not be parsed
input.unparseable_certificate.explanation: This block is framed as a certificate, but the X.509 parser rejected it. Its fingerprints are computed from the bytes where possible; none of its other fields are shown, because none can be relied on.

remediation.text: Obtain a correctly encoded certificate from its issuer.

input.malformed_spki.title: Malformed public key
input.malformed_spki.explanation: The certificate's public key is not a valid encoding for the algorithm it declares, so it has no x509-spki-sha256 key identity.

remediation.text: Obtain a correctly encoded certificate from its issuer.

cert.expired.title: Certificate has expired
cert.expired.explanation: The inspection time is after the certificate's notAfter date. Software that validates certificates will reject it.

remediation.text: Renew or replace the certificate, then deploy the replacement everywhere the old one is used.

cert.not_yet_valid.title: Certificate is not yet valid
cert.not_yet_valid.explanation: The inspection time is before the certificate's notBefore date, so validation fails until then. A wrong system clock can cause the same result.

remediation.text: Check the clock of the machine that validates the certificate.
If the dates are wrong, reissue the certificate with the intended validity period.

cert.expiring_soon.title: Certificate expires soon
cert.expiring_soon.explanation: The certificate expires within 30 days (within 7 days is critical).

remediation.text: Renew the certificate and deploy the replacement before the old one expires.

cert.self_signed_leaf.title: Self-signed end-entity certificate
cert.self_signed_leaf.explanation: The certificate is not a CA certificate and is signed by its own key. Clients accept it only if they are configured to accept this specific certificate; it is not issued by any certificate authority.

remediation.text: Issue the certificate from a private or public CA that the clients already trust.

sig.sha1.title: SHA-1 signature
sig.sha1.explanation: The certificate is signed with SHA-1, which is no longer collision resistant, and current software rejects SHA-1 certificate signatures. On a self-signed CA certificate the signature is not checked when that certificate is used as a trust anchor, so there it is informational.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with a SHA-256 or stronger signature.

sig.md5.title: MD5 signature
sig.md5.explanation: The certificate is signed with MD5, which is broken, and certificate signatures using it can be forged. On a self-signed CA certificate the signature is not checked when that certificate is used as a trust anchor, so there it is informational.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with a SHA-256 or stronger signature.

key.rsa_under_2048.title: RSA key shorter than 2048 bits
key.rsa_under_2048.explanation: RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits are considered too weak, and current software and policies reject them.

remediation.text: Generate a new key of at least 2048 bits (or an ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519 key) and reissue the certificate.

key.noncanonical_spki.title: Public key has a non-canonical encoding
key.noncanonical_spki.explanation: The public key is encoded differently from its canonical form, for example RSA without NULL parameters or a compressed EC point. Its x509-spki-sha256 identity uses the canonical form, so the as-encoded fingerprint differs and is shown separately. Some software rejects such encodings.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with a canonically encoded public key.

key.unsupported_for_identity.title: No key identity for this key type
key.unsupported_for_identity.explanation: This key algorithm or encoding is outside ADR-0002, so it has no x509-spki-sha256 identity and cannot be matched with other files. Its as-encoded fingerprint is still shown.

name.cn_only_no_san.title: Name is only in the Common Name
name.cn_only_no_san.explanation: The certificate names its subject only in the Common Name and has no Subject Alternative Name extension. Modern TLS clients ignore the Common Name when they match host names.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with its names in the Subject Alternative Name extension.

name.hostname_mismatch.title: Certificate does not identify the requested host name
name.hostname_mismatch.explanation: None of the certificate's subject alternative names identifies the host name or IP address requested with --hostname. Matching uses Go's crypto/x509 host name verification: DNS names match without regard to ASCII case, a wildcard matches only as the whole left-most label, an IP address matches only IP address entries, and the Common Name is never used. This concerns identity only; trust and purpose are separate questions.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with the host name or IP address in its Subject Alternative Name extension, or check that the intended host name was requested.

issuer.candidate_unverifiable.title: Issuer certificate found, but its signature could not be checked
issuer.candidate_unverifiable.explanation: A certificate in this input matches this certificate's issuer, but the signature could not be checked with its key, for example because the signature algorithm is one the verification engine refuses. This is not evidence that the signature is invalid, and none of the input's certificates was confirmed as the issuer.

remediation.text: If the certificate is still in use, reissue it with a signature algorithm current software accepts.

chain.issuer_not_ca.title: Issuer is not a CA certificate
chain.issuer_not_ca.explanation: A certificate in this input verifies another certificate's signature, but it is not a CA certificate: its BasicConstraints extension is missing or does not set CA:TRUE. Certification path validation does not accept such a certificate as the issuer of another certificate. The signature itself still verifies.

remediation.text: Issue the certificate from a certificate marked as a CA (BasicConstraints CA:TRUE).

chain.issuer_key_usage.title: Issuer's key usage does not allow certificate signing
chain.issuer_key_usage.explanation: An issuer certificate on a path has a KeyUsage extension without keyCertSign, so certification path validation does not accept it as the issuer of another certificate.

remediation.text: Reissue the CA certificate with keyCertSign in its KeyUsage extension.

chain.path_length_exceeded.title: Path length constraint exceeded
chain.path_length_exceeded.explanation: A CA certificate's pathLenConstraint allows fewer intermediate CA certificates below it than this path contains. Self-issued intermediate certificates are not counted.

remediation.text: Issue the lower certificates from a CA whose path length constraint allows this depth, or use fewer intermediate CAs.

chain.structure_unverifiable.title: Path structure could not be fully verified
chain.structure_unverifiable.explanation: Trustsmith checked the issuers on this path (CA status, key usage and path length) and found no violation, but the path also contains something this version does not evaluate, such as a critical extension it does not process, name or policy constraints on an issuer, or a version 1 issuer. The structure is therefore reported as structurally unverifiable, never as satisfied.

chain.cycle.title: Issuer relationships form a cycle
chain.cycle.explanation: Following verified issuer relationships in this input leads back to a certificate already on the path, so path construction stopped there.

remediation.text: Check how these certificates were issued; a cycle usually means certificates that signed each other are both included.

chain.path_limit_reached.title: Not all certification paths were built
chain.path_limit_reached.explanation: This input allows more certification paths, or longer ones, than Trustsmith builds for one inspection. The paths shown are incomplete, not a full list.

remediation.text: Inspect a smaller bundle that contains only the certificates of interest.

trust.failed.title: Not verified against the supplied roots
trust.failed.explanation: Trustsmith asked Go's crypto/x509 verifier to validate this certificate against the trust anchors supplied with --roots, and the verifier rejected it. The reason evidence is a stable code, such as no_explicit_anchor_path or certificate_expired. Only the supplied roots were considered: no system trust store was used, and certificates in the inspected input are never anchors themselves.

remediation.text: Check that the roots file holds the intended trust anchors and that the inspected input includes the intermediate certificates the chain needs.

trust.unverifiable.title: Validation against the supplied roots was inconclusive
trust.unverifiable.explanation: Go's crypto/x509 verifier did not reach a conclusion Trustsmith can classify, for example because a work limit was reached. This is not evidence that the certificate would be rejected or accepted.

purpose.eku_disallows_usage.title: Extended key usage does not permit the requested purpose
purpose.eku_disallows_usage.explanation: The certificate's extended key usage extension lists specific usages, and neither the usage the purpose requested with --purpose needs nor anyExtendedKeyUsage is among them. Software that checks extended key usage refuses the certificate for that purpose. This concerns the certificate's own fields only; trust and host names are separate questions.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with the extended key usage the purpose needs, or check that the intended purpose was requested.

purpose.key_usage_disallows_usage.title: Key usage does not permit the requested purpose
purpose.key_usage_disallows_usage.explanation: The certificate's key usage extension sets none of the key usage bits RFC 5280 names as consistent with the purpose requested with --purpose. Go's certificate verifier does not check a certificate's key usage bits for this, but other software may refuse the certificate.

remediation.text: Reissue the certificate with a key usage consistent with the purpose, or check that the intended purpose was requested.

issuer.candidates_not_checked.title: Some possible issuers were not checked
issuer.candidates_not_checked.explanation: This input contains more possible issuer certificates than Trustsmith checks for one certificate or for one input, so some were not checked. The issuer information shown for this certificate is incomplete, not absent.

remediation.text: Inspect a smaller bundle that contains only the certificates of interest.
